title: Last time Reddit said my game was crap 😅 So I worked on it — here’s attempt #2 (free browser demo)
author: SeaworthinessFit6280
selftext:
Hi everyone!

A week ago I posted my fishing game here and the verdict was pretty unanimous: it’s crap. Fair enough 😄 So I didn’t give up. I took the feedback and kept working on it, and now I’m back for round two.

**Relax Fishing** is a small, calm fishing game for phones. I’m planning to release it on the App Store and Google Play. For now there’s a free demo on [itch.io](http://itch.io) that runs right in your browser, on desktop and mobile.

**Full honesty again:** I have zero programming experience. Everything is made in Unity with AI help: Claude for the code, ChatGPT for the graphics. I know that’s not popular here, so I’m saying it upfront.

**What I’m asking:** if you have 5–10 minutes, give it a try and tell me honestly: is it still crap, or is it worth finishing and releasing on mobile? What you liked, what annoyed you, what’s missing, what broke. Brutal is fine, it helps more than “nice” 🙂

👉 [https://kholodniuk.itch.io/relax-fishing](https://kholodniuk.itch.io/relax-fishing)

Thanks for your time!

comments.author: Cubey42
comments.body: Anyone else think people just saying (x hated it) as a marketing angle now? Like isn't this account brand new?

replies.author: SeaworthinessFit6280
replies.body: Not a marketing trick, I promise 😅 I'm not a company, just one guy with zero coding experience. My first post about this game was on r/aigamedev and r/IndieGaming last week, and most comments said it was slop. That's honestly why I came back with an update instead of giving up. The account is new because I only started posting when I started this game.

replies.author: SeaworthinessFit6280
replies.body: Thanks, that's actually really useful. What happened in those 12 seconds? Was it the language/name screen, the tutorial, or waiting for the first bite? I want to fix whatever lost you first.

replies.author: SeaworthinessFit6280
replies.body: True! That's kind of the plan — a small game for people who like calm fishing, not for everyone. Do you think the niche is big enough on mobile, or too small to bother?

replies.author: SeaworthinessFit6280
replies.body:
Thanks for your comment last time! I've updated the game based on the feedback — new mechanics, shop, locations and graphics fixes. Would be grateful if you gave it another try and let me know what you think 🎣  
[https://kholodniuk.itch.io/relax-fishing](https://kholodniuk.itch.io/relax-fishing)

replies.author: Schnitzhole
replies.body: Cheers and looking forward to see any updates you make. I can’t stand all the hate and low effort responses people on here give all the time. I know I come off as a bit blunt but I give the kind of feedback I would want but never get (I’m mainly an app, web, and graphic designer but dabbled in gamemaking since I was a teen)

replies.author: SeaworthinessFit6280
replies.body: Blunt is exactly what I need, honestly. Polite "looks nice" comments don't help me fix anything. Your notes went straight onto my to-do list. I'll ping you when the update is out. Thanks again!

comments.author: marin_04
comments.body:
I feel you need more content here and I feel like I am playing LMB simulator. I get it that this should be a cozy game, but I feel like I am missing excitement and challenge after catching a fish. Also, I just keep LMB pressed and being always to catch a fish. Also, menu misses tooltips, it was hard for me to distinguish what is what by merely just looking into icons.   
  
Maybe take a look into this game: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=o8KwWSOY5kE](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=o8KwWSOY5kE)  
  
It should maybe give you a better feedback how to create a fishing mechanic a little bit more fun and rewarding even tho it is a different game in general. Also, I am missing depth in the screen itself and general feedback in dropping a bait. I feel like that holding a LMB to drop bait further would be better than just click or press where you want to drop it. With graphics I have no general issue, but it didn't just clicked with me. I feel like game like this would click better with some different style. 

Just don't give up. Continue developing and no worries. Feedback is important

replies.author: SeaworthinessFit6280
replies.body: Thanks a lot, this is super helpful! You and another commenter both nailed the same thing: reeling is too easy, just hold and win. I'm reworking the fish fight so you actually have to react, plus labels on the menu and a power cast. I'll check out the video too. Thanks for the encouragement! 🙏

replies.author: marin_04
replies.body: No worries. Today it is easier to create a game, but it is hard to create a good game. Everything is a part of a learning process. Don't let feedback discourage you but rather take it as a part of the process. No one became great at doing stuff over the night.

replies.author: SeaworthinessFit6280
replies.body: Thanks, really appreciate that. This thread taught me more in one evening than a week of building alone. Back to work on the fish fight! 💪

comments.author: xavium
comments.body:
Well done for not giving up! It's got a way to go though. 

For me this plays a bit too much like a mobile advert. It feels too still, and the gameplay is too simple. 

I'm an avid carp fisher and for me, to take this to another level, the visuals need to hit. It needs animation, a proper style (doesn't have to be realistic!), and something I'd like to look at. Once the visuals, style and gameplay are nailed, there's so much depth you could add. Rigs, rods, lines, baits, groundbaits, etc. 

The menus are difficult to see and navigate, the UI is a little too basic, and the actions/gameplay mechanics don't feel very satisfying or new/unique.

If I was to try and take somewhere I'd spend a fair amount of time trying to mood board/storyboard concept art and styles to find something that looks good to me and feels unique, then look at how to get that into the game. Then I'd rework and experiment with a lot of different gameplay mechanic ideas. Then I'd polish it quite a bit before adding any depth like shops, equipment, chat, achievements, tutorial, etc. 

Get the main gameplay loop working well first then add stuff. Tutorial should be the very last before release, or you end up with it being out of date after every pass.

replies.author: SeaworthinessFit6280
replies.body: Thanks, this is a really thorough comment! You're right: I've been adding breadth (shop, market, chat) while the core loop is still flat. I'm stopping new features and focusing on making the cast, bite, fight and catch feel alive first, then I'll work on finding a proper style. Great tip about leaving the tutorial for last. I'll try to get a better version out in a few weeks. Tight lines! 🎣

replies.author: xavium
replies.body: Your motivation is fantastic, keep it up and keep learning! Tight lines!

replies.author: SeaworthinessFit6280
replies.body: Thanks a lot, really appreciate it!

replies.author: xavium
replies.body: One more thing I didn't mention but could be helpful - personally I'd step back from unity. It does a bit too much for what you might need. I'd recommend pixi or threejs, they run very well in the browser and have great capability, and the AI finds it easier to work with pure JavaScript or typescript anyway. Give it a look, it'll take out a lot of complexity.

replies.author: SeaworthinessFit6280
replies.body:
Hey, I followed your advice and focused on the core loop instead of adding features. The cast now has an accuracy meter. The fight has surges, line slip and species-specific behaviour, and you can actually lose the fish. There's a landing net moment and a proper catch card at the end. Visuals are still a work in progress, but I'd love an opinion from a real carp fisher on whether the fight feels better now. Tight lines! 🎣  
[https://kholodniuk.itch.io/relax-fishing](https://kholodniuk.itch.io/relax-fishing)

replies.author: xavium
replies.body: Nice work! Feels lots better to me, keep going with it :)
